text: That evening, in the gathering darkness: Holmes has scruples about taking Watson to-night
why: ¶196 states Holmes says this as they sit in the gathering darkness, on the evening of the visit.

text: What is the danger that Holmes expects to-night?
why: Holmes has just said there is a distinct element of danger to-night; the question is plain and does not point to an answer.

text: What is the danger that Holmes expects to-night? — whatever reached Julia in that room
id: q.what_danger=whatever reached Julia in that room
why: They will spend the night in the room where Julia died and Holmes suspects a tangible cause, so this is a natural possibility that adds no new detail.

text: What is the danger that Holmes expects to-night? — Dr. Roylott's strength and temper, if he finds them there
id: q.what_danger=Dr. Roylott's strength and temper, if he finds them there
why: Roylott's strength and violent temper are well established, and he threatened Holmes, so a reader has reason to consider this.

text: What is the danger that Holmes expects to-night? — the cheetah and the baboon loose on the grounds
id: q.what_danger=the cheetah and the baboon loose on the grounds
why: The story says the cheetah and baboon wander freely over the grounds, and the sisters locked their doors because of them.

text: What is the danger that Holmes expects to-night? — the gipsies in the plantation
why: The gipsies camp in the plantation, are intimate with Roylott, and feature in Holmes's own theory, so this is a reasonable possibility.
